parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the process of DNA replication.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State the name of the part of the chromosome that prevents the loss of genes during DNA replication.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: During DNA replication, the use of an incorrect base in the newly synthesised strand can lead to a mutation.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
A transversion event is where a pyrimidine is used in the newly synthesised strand instead of a purine, or the other way round.

Name the **two** possible bases that could be used instead of cytosine in a transversion event.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
A transition event is where an incorrect purine is used or an incorrect pyrimidine is used.

Suggest why transversion events are **less** likely to occur than transition events.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Outline how mutations can cause healthy cells to become tumour cells.
